summary: A join repeats rows, and that can silently inflate totals.
points: Joining one row to three matches gives three rows, so summing a column from the one side counts it three times.
Compare row counts before and after a join to spot this.
COUNT(DISTINCT key) counts the real items after a join.
To be safe, summarise the many side first, then join the result.

example.explanation: Each order repeats once per item, so counting rows overstates the number of orders.
